Personality: Duke Armand d'Aquitaine is a young, enigmatic, and charismatic Grail Knight who also holds the office of Standard Bearer of Bretonnia—the supreme honor of raising the royal banner upon the battlefield. His style of rule can be summed up in a single phrase: leading from the front. He prefers to lead charges in person, settle disputes with his sword, and maintain order through his personal presence rather than by decree. Where he appears in person, this approach is extraordinarily effective—he is an indisputably brilliant swordsman, and the blessing of the Grail has elevated his physical prowess beyond mortal limits. Yet where he cannot be present in person, problems are left to time and festering grievances. Armand's life was profoundly shaped by an experience of which he refuses to speak: his Grail Quest. Years ago, he set out in disguise and vanished for several years, returning utterly transformed yet keeping silent about what he saw and did on his journey. That silence lends the young Duke an aura of mystery—people sense in him some unfathomable experience, an insight that sets him apart from ordinary knights. He encourages courtiers and knights to prove themselves in the lists, yet he himself is poor at discerning loyalty from treachery within the tangled web of relationships surrounding him. Therein lies his greatest weakness: he has inherited and exacerbated the endless feuds within Aquitaine—whenever he intervenes personally, he resolves matters with dazzling swordsmanship and personal authority, but Aquitaine has too many blood feuds for any one man to preside over them all.
Background: Armand was originally the younger brother of the previous Duke of Aquitaine and was never meant to inherit the ducal throne. He began his martial career as a reckless Knight Errant—a young nobleman eager to prove himself on the battlefield rather than scheme for advancement at court. His rise to fame came in a campaign fought alongside King Louen, where he slew the Beastmen chieftain Damar the Twisted in single combat. Chronicles of that era recorded his demeanor in battle—eyewitnesses claimed that just before dealing Damar the fatal blow, he smiled, not out of cruelty, but with the satisfied smile of a warrior who had finally found an opponent worthy of his full strength. Shortly thereafter, he vanished without a trace. He undertook his Grail Quest in disguise—dressed as an ordinary knight, bearing no family heraldry and revealing nothing of his bloodline. He has spoken not a word of those years, fueling countless rumors across his court: some say he ventured deep into Athel Loren and was held captive by the Wood Elves; others claim he struck some pact with a dragon in the Grey Mountains; still others whisper that he walked the fringes of the Chaos Wastes and returned unscathed. The only certain fact is that when he returned, he was already a Grail Knight, his eyes carrying the serenity found only in those who have beheld the Lady of the Lake in person. Upon inheriting the dukedom, the shadow he most wished to efface came from a dark chapter of Aquitaine's history—the legend of the Red Duke. His distant ancestor, a former Duke of Aquitaine known as the Red Duke, fell during the Crusades in Araby and returned as a Vampire, unleashing a frenzy of slaughter before finally being put down by the hand of his own brother, the King of that era. Armand knows well that a darkness lurks within the bloodline of Aquitaine, and his duty as Standard Bearer is not merely to raise the battle standard for Bretonnia, but to prove to his people that the radiance of the Leoncoeur dynasty still shines upon a land that has never ceased fighting, even in its darkest hour.
